title: Patchline: customer lens & priority threading
body:
TL;DR:
A compact synthesis of field signals collected Nov 2025–Jan 2026 across support threads, CSM interviews, and runtime telemetry. Purpose: create a thin prioritization strand (the "patchline") that groups high-frequency customer asks with viable engineering patches and measurable cost impact.

Methodology (notes to self):
- Source mix: 42 support tickets flagged high-impact, 6 enterprise customer interviews, annotated traces from serving-runtime (latency & kv-cache misses).
- Heuristic: frequency * customer-value * implementation lift (approx). We sketched cost delta using estimated token-ops and kv-cache hit improvement assumptions.
- Caveats: signals biased toward customers with dedicated deployments (more debug visibility). Smaller self-serve users under-represented.

Top threads (ranked):
1) Persistent small-latency regressions for conversational sticky sessions (esp when using long KV cache keys).
   - Ask: reduce tail latency spikes during long chat sessions and when switching model variants.
   - Customer impact: chatbots degrade, perceived flakiness, aborted sessions.
   - Proposed patch: improve kv-cache eviction heuristics + add optional per-session priority lanes for KV hot-keys (config flag in Dedicated).
   - Rough cost impact: 4–7% token cost saving for heavy chatters when hit-rate improves, ~S-medium engineering (2–3 sprint weeks).

2) Ambiguous fallback behavior when primary model is overloaded (customers want deterministic routing and observable policy).
   - Ask: clearer API-level indicators and opt-in deterministic fallback presets.
   - Customer impact: unexpected model changes during peak, debug churn.
   - Proposed patch: expose fallback_reason in response metadata; add a routing_policy=stable option that pins variant unless explicit capacity failover.
   - Rough cost: minimal infra change, product + SDK docs work.

3) Embedding mismatch (small differences between hosted/quantized variants causing downstream retraining loops).
   - Ask: consistent embedding drift quant reporting, or migration helpers.
   - Customer impact: search/semantic match quality regressions post-quantization.
   - Proposed patch: embedding-consistency check endpoint + migration-report artifact (CSV) for affected index.
   - Rough cost: medium; requires model-variant diff harness (research/AMLR).

4) Developer ergonomics: unclear per-request cost breakdown (tokens vs model variant vs caching).
   - Ask: token-level cost attribution in Console + SDK sample response.
   - Customer impact: teams overprovision or avoid caching optimizations.
   - Proposed patch: small console UI change + response-header X-Redwood-UnitCost breakdown prototype.
   - Rough cost: low; quick win for hosted customers.

5) Canary rollouts: difficulty validating quality regressions on real prompts (customers want guardrails).
   - Ask: rollout policies that support prompt-set evaluations and automatic rollback triggers.
   - Customer impact: rolling new model variants is risky for conversation quality.
   - Proposed patch: add eval-hook to rollout pipeline; integrate with Optimize prompt-sets and quality check thresholds.
   - Rough cost: medium; cross-product work (Deploy + Optimize).

6) Private deployment onboarding friction: network & KMS configuration surprises (air-gap customers).
   - Ask: concise environment checklist + deterministic troubleshooting runbook.
   - Customer impact: long provisioning times, support ping-pong.
   - Proposed patch: condensed onboarding checklist doc + sample Terraform + KMS mapping template.
   - Rough cost: low; documentation + 1-off engineering support artifact.

Representative vignettes (short):
- Vignette A (enterprise fintech): repeated session truncation after 2h; root cause traced to suboptimal KV eviction during multi-turn summaries. Raised CS-9876. Wants per-session pinning.
- Vignette B (marketplace analytics): embedding drift after switching to int8 variant -> search recall drop 8–12%. Blocking migration.
- Vignette C (gaming startup): rollout caused sudden hallucination spike; they had no prompt-eval gating.

Tradeoffs and detection signals:
- KV-cache heuristics: faster eviction reduces mem pressure but increases misses. We should instrument hit-rate per-session and provide a toggle for experimental priority lanes.
- Deterministic fallback: reduces surprise but may worsen latency if pinned to higher-cost region; recommend opt-in.
- Embedding checks: require sample re-encoding budget; may add latency to migration flows.

Quick wins (<=2 sprints):
- Add fallback_reason in response metadata (API + SDK change). Owner: product-hosted-api + SDK.
- Console: add basic unit-cost column to request inspector. Owner: console-and-rollouts.
- Private deploy: publish onboarding checklist + Terraform snippet. Owner: private-deployments docs + SE.

Medium-term experiments (2–8 sprints):
- KV priority lane PoC (evaluate on two large customers). Owner: serving-runtime + platform-engineering.
- Embedding diff harness and migration CSV artifact. Owner: applied-ml + optimize.
- Rollout eval-hook integrated with Optimize and automatic rollback. Owner: product-rollouts + optimize.

Metrics to track (proposed):
- Percent of sessions with kv-cache hit-rate > 90% (by customer tier).
- Number of surprise fallbacks per 10k requests.
- Embedding recall delta pre/post migration.
- Time-to-onboard (private customers) from first ticket to production.

Immediate next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: spin up lightweight KV hit-rate dashboard column (CS telemetry). Due: 2026-02-12.
- Marco: prototype response metadata flag for fallback_reason and draft SDK change. Due: 2026-02-05.
- Priya: create onboarding checklist doc and Terraform mapping; schedule sample call with two air-gap customers. Due: 2026-02-09.

Open questions & discussion points (for product sync):
- How aggressive do we want automatic fallback pinning to be by default?
- Can we offer a hosted migration SLA for embeddings to reduce customer migration friction (possible revenue stream)?
- Should Optimize include a "compatibility score" for embedding variant swaps?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; I prioritized actionable asks and low-friction patches that reduce customer hair-on-fire moments. Want feedback on estimated lift numbers (esp. kv priority lane).
- Slack thread with raw field notes: #cs-field-notes (see linked_artifacts).

Appendix (raw snippets):
- "If we roll this model during peak the search suddenly returned worse results and we had to rollback — we had no visibility into why." — customer excerpt from ticket 11234.
- "Session latency increases only after ~45 minutes of continuous chat, then it spikes — feels like memory leak or cache thrash." — CS interview notes.

End.
